receiptVerification.description: OFFLINE receipt-verification golden vectors for Agreely.verifyReceipt / Agreely::verifyReceipt. Both the TS and PHP SDKs assert these BYTE-IDENTICALLY (the same JCS canonicalizer, multibase decode, Ed25519 + WebAuthn/COSE verification). Tests inject a resolver (from `didDocuments`) and an IPFS fetch (from `ipfsBody`): no network. A company-attested receipt is fully offline-sound; a citizen receipt is honestly PARTIAL offline (companySignature unsupported: the company half signed the OFFER and travels only in the verification bundle, which this verifier does not read). documentAnchor is skipped offline (no rpcUrl). A case with resolveDids "none" simulates an unresolvable DID (outage): the decisive check is "unavailable" and overall is "unavailable" (inconclusive), NEVER "failed" (a tamper).

Both SDKs assert these against a mocked transport: the POST /v1/consent-requests body carries customerId + recipientEmail + validUntil + EXACTLY ONE of consentDocumentId / documentCode (the Law 25 s. 8 information document reference), and NEVER an `items` list (items derive from the document server-side; a caller-supplied list is dropped by the SDK and rejected by the API). bundleVerification.description: Receipt AND verification-bundle golden vectors from GENUINE dev artefacts and the forgeries of QA pass qa-ver1 (vectors/receipts/). Both SDKs assert these byte-identically. A case reads `file` (relative to vectors/), resolves DIDs from receipts/did-documents.json (resolveDids true) or from nothing ("none"). A case with `ipfsFile` (the exact pinned bytes, relative to vectors/) or `ipfsBody` (served as its JSON) turns verifyDisclosure on, with ipfsGateways [] and the gateway https://ipfs.test/ipfs/ as ipfsGateway, which serves those bytes for any CID. f7-issuer.bundle.json and f11-basis.bundle.json are the genuine A1 v1 and A1 v2 bundles with their receipt replaced by the forged receipt of the same name. A case with `chain` reads on that chainId and registryAddress through an rpcUrl that answers by selector: every eth_call registry(bytes32) answers `registryAnswer`, every companyKeyOf(bytes32,bytes32) `companyKeyOfAnswer`, and any other call is refused, with the verifier's clock pinned at `now` (unix seconds): a1v1 names that registry in its delegation.
